Text: The three phases of JVM classloading are **{{c1::Loading}}**, **{{c2::Linking}}**, and **{{c3::Initialization}}**.
Extra: The classloader performs these dynamically and on-demand as classes are first referenced at runtime.

Text: The three steps of the classloading Linking phase are **{{c1::Verification}}**, **{{c2::Preparation}}**, and **{{c3::Resolution}}**.
Extra: Verification checks bytecode safety. Preparation allocates static memory and zero-fills it. Resolution maps symbolic pointers to direct pointers.

Text: The **{{c1::Bootstrap}}** ClassLoader is written in native code and is represented by `null` in the Java API.
Extra: It is responsible for loading the core runtime libraries (like `java.lang.Object`) from the platform base module.

Text: In Java 9+, the Extension ClassLoader was replaced by the **{{c1::Platform}}** ClassLoader.
Extra: It loads platform-specific SE specification classes that are not part of the core base module (like SQL or XML utilities).

Text: In Java's classloading **{{c1::parent delegation}}** model, a loader delegates class requests to its parent before searching itself.
Extra: This protects core classes from being shadowed or overridden by user-supplied libraries.

Text: Class runtime identity is defined by the fully qualified name and the **{{c1::defining ClassLoader instance}}**.
Extra: A class loaded by two different classloaders represents two separate class types in JVM memory.

Text: To load application classes from core platform libraries, Java uses the **{{c1::Thread Context ClassLoader}}** (TCCL) to break parent delegation.
Extra: This is crucial for Service Provider Interface (SPI) libraries such as JDBC.

Text: Class metadata, method bytecode, and constant pool information are stored in **{{c1::Metaspace}}**, which uses native OS memory.
Extra: In Java 8, Metaspace replaced PermGen. Repeated classloading without unloading leads to Metaspace leaks.
